purpose: Evidence for improving material tracking, contact-address inference, and independent finite-element validation in soft-cutting videos.
policy: Primary sources only. Public PDFs are local reading copies, excluded from Git. A public URL does not imply redistribution rights. No experimental data, model weights or credentials are uploaded. No papers are presented as validating oil-contaminated blade-contact measurements in this repository.

entries.title: A Good Practices Guide for Digital Image Correlation, Edition 2
entries.evidence_scope: Official guide page verifies edition, scope and citation; full Edition 2 not downloaded because official access uses a registration form.
entries.relevance: Plan image acquisition, reporting, displacement/strain processing and validation before comparing algorithms.
entries.limitation: Scope is common laboratory DIC; it does not certify this project's contact, oil, occlusion or large-compression estimates.
entries.rights: Official page permits unaltered distribution with full attribution; no form was submitted on the user's behalf.

entries.title: A Good Practices Guide for Digital Image Correlation
entries.evidence_scope: Official first-edition PDF and copyright page.
entries.relevance: Immediately available practical background on image quality, setup, calibration and uncertainty.
entries.limitation: Superseded by the 2025 second edition; retained as an accessible reading copy, not described as the latest guide.
entries.rights: Copyright iDICs 2018; unaltered reproduction with full attribution permitted by guide.

entries.title: DIC Challenge 2.0: Developing Images and Guidelines for Evaluating Accuracy and Resolution of 2D Analyses: Focus on the Metrological Efficiency Indicator
entries.evidence_scope: Publisher abstract, date and bibliographic record; publisher full text requires subscription.
entries.relevance: Measure noise together with effective spatial resolution; use standardized synthetic images to distinguish smoothing from real accuracy gains.
entries.limitation: Challenge patterns do not reproduce severe blade occlusion or liquid interference. Benchmark gains must be retested on local imagery.
entries.rights: Publisher subscription article; link only; no paywall bypass.

entries.title: Complete mechanical regularization applied to digital image and volume correlation
entries.venue: Computer Methods in Applied Mechanics and Engineering 355, 27–43
entries.evidence_scope: Publisher abstract and bibliographic record; not a full-text review.
entries.relevance: Treat interior and boundary conditions distinctly when regularizing a displacement field.
entries.limitation: The stated reference behavior is linear elastic. This is not a ready-made finite-strain hyperelastic contact/sliding model.
entries.rights: Publisher article; no verified open PDF downloaded.

entries.title: Finite strain formulation of the discrete equilibrium gap principle: application to mechanically consistent regularization for large motion tracking
entries.evidence_scope: Publisher open article, abstract, license and full PDF.
entries.relevance: Finite-strain equilibrium-gap regularization and boundary traction treatment motivate an optional mechanically consistent branch.
entries.limitation: Published demonstrations on synthetic motion/noise do not establish accuracy for cutting, occlusion, oil or crack initiation. Constitutive assumptions introduce bias.
entries.rights: CC BY 4.0; publisher states authors retain copyright.

entries.title: From pictures to extended finite elements: extended digital image correlation (X-DIC)
entries.evidence_scope: Publisher abstract, bibliographic record and openly served archived PDF.
entries.relevance: Enriched displacement representations can keep opposing sides of a sliding interface independent.
entries.limitation: Bolted-interface slip demonstration; no direct validation of rubber fracture onset or original-surface contact identity.
entries.rights: Public publisher archive reading copy; redistribution license not asserted.

entries.title: A Novel Subset Splitting Procedure for Digital Image Correlation on Discontinuous Displacement Fields
entries.evidence_scope: Author-laboratory PDF and author institution bibliographic record.
entries.relevance: Local subsets spanning a discontinuity should be split or selected on one side instead of enforcing one affine motion.
entries.limitation: Recovering hidden texture is not achieved by splitting; available pixels and discontinuity geometry remain limiting.
entries.rights: Author-laboratory hosted reading copy; original publisher copyright retained, redistribution license not asserted.

entries.title: The fracture mechanics in cutting: A comparative study on hard and soft polymeric materials
entries.evidence_scope: Publisher abstract and author-university record; no full PDF obtained.
entries.relevance: Directly relevant cutting experiments combine insertion force and full-field finite-strain DIC; blade tip and crack tip must be distinguished.
entries.limitation: Steady cutting and tested polymers do not provide a universal threshold or prove the same onset/sliding behavior in these oblique rubber experiments.
entries.rights: Publisher article; no verified open PDF downloaded.

entries.title: Why cutting is easier than tearing elastomers
entries.evidence_scope: Publisher and PubMed abstract/bibliographic record; public PDF retrieval returned an HTML access challenge. No access challenge bypassed.
entries.relevance: Use independent molecular-damage evidence to separate cutting physics from simple geometric motion arguments.
entries.limitation: PDMS and mechanofluorophore experiments; intensity or visible recoil in this repository is not a molecular-damage measurement.
entries.rights: Open-access article; exact downloaded-copy license must be checked before redistribution.
entries.download_error: Public URL did not return a PDF; no HTML challenge saved

entries.title: Validation of finite-element models using full-field experimental data: Levelling finite-element analysis data through a digital image correlation engine
entries.evidence_scope: Publisher abstract, bibliographic record and conclusions in the accessible abstract; no full PDF obtained.
entries.relevance: Compare FE and experiment after matching coordinates, strain definitions, data locations, spatial resolution and filtering; synthetic-image levelling is a useful check.
entries.limitation: Matching the measurement operator removes a comparison artifact; it does not prove the constitutive model or contact law is correct.
entries.rights: Publisher article; no verified open PDF downloaded.

entries.title: TAP-Vid: A Benchmark for Tracking Any Point in a Video
entries.evidence_scope: Authors' arXiv paper and benchmark description.
entries.relevance: Separate tracking position accuracy, occlusion and physical point identity across long sequences.
entries.limitation: AJ and pixel thresholds on general scenes are not a micrometre uncertainty statement for rubber.
entries.rights: Author arXiv reading copy; follow paper-specific arXiv license, no redistribution assumption.

entries.title: TAPIR: Tracking Any Point with Per-Frame Initialization and Temporal Refinement
entries.evidence_scope: Authors' paper and official DeepMind publication page.
entries.relevance: Independent framewise matching plus temporal refinement provides alternative candidates when sequential local matching drifts.
entries.limitation: A learned candidate still requires local image, blade-exclusion and identity checks; occluded predictions are not observations.
entries.rights: CVF public reading copy; copyright retained by authors or other holders under CVF terms.

entries.title: BootsTAP: Bootstrapped Training for Tracking-Any-Point
entries.evidence_scope: Authors' arXiv and accepted conference paper.
entries.relevance: Shows that real-video training distribution matters, even without replacing the tracking architecture.
entries.limitation: This is a training strategy; this project is not deploying the large-scale training procedure or claiming adaptation to oil.
entries.rights: CVF public reading copy; copyright retained by authors or other holders under CVF terms.

entries.title: CoTracker3: Simpler and Better Point Tracking by Pseudo-Labelling Real Videos
entries.evidence_scope: Official project, authors' preprint and accepted ICCV 2025 paper.
entries.relevance: Online/offline point tracking with joint context and visibility/confidence is a useful independent proposal source.
entries.limitation: Joint tracking may transfer the wrong body's motion across blade/material interfaces. Confidence is not locally calibrated metrological uncertainty.
entries.rights: CVF public reading copy. Official code and deployed checkpoint: CC-BY-NC-4.0; separately licensed upstream components retained.

deployment.temporal_scope: Offline: uses future frames only inside supplied cutoff-bounded window.
deployment.evidence_semantics: Visibility/confidence are model predictions, not observed material identities. Independent image checks are required.

entries.title: TAPNext: Tracking Any Point (TAP) as Next Token Prediction
entries.evidence_scope: Accepted ICCV 2025 paper and authors' arXiv record.
entries.relevance: Causal online tracking is relevant to estimates that must not use post-fracture future frames.
entries.limitation: Benchmark claims are general-video claims; causal design alone does not ensure correct surface identity or compressed-texture accuracy.
entries.rights: CVF public reading copy; copyright retained by authors or other holders under CVF terms.

entries.title: TAPNext++: What's Next for Tracking Any Point (TAP)?
entries.venue: CVPR 2026 Findings (official project and authors arXiv record)
entries.evidence_scope: Authors arXiv abstract and full HTML paper (methods and benchmark tables), official project, pinned PyTorch implementation/demo, Google model card and published checkpoint hash.
entries.relevance: Causal long-sequence tracking and re-detection after occlusion provide a directly relevant candidate for lost material identities. Official existing weights can be tested without training.
entries.limitation: General-video benchmark gains vary by dataset and metric; they do not establish precision under rubber compression, liquid interference or cutting. The 256 deployment is not the separate 512 fine-tuned variant. Short execution smoke does not validate long-horizon recovery.
entries.rights: Paper: CC-BY-4.0 per arXiv HTML. Official code and Google checkpoint model card: Apache-2.0.

deployment.temporal_scope: Frame-by-frame causal inference, first-frame queries, state reset per supplied window.
deployment.evidence_semantics: Visibility is a predicted probability; positional confidence is not emitted (NaN). Independent image checks are required.

entries.title: RAFT: Recurrent All-Pairs Field Transforms for Optical Flow
entries.evidence_scope: Authors' arXiv paper and official code repository.
entries.relevance: A standard dense optical-flow reference and possible initialization source for larger image displacements.
entries.limitation: Pairwise dense flow is not long-term material identity; composing flow accumulates error and does not identify hidden material.
entries.rights: Author arXiv reading copy; follow paper-specific license; code and weight rights are separate.

entries.title: Cutting soft materials: how material differences shape the response
entries.evidence_scope: Publisher and PubMed bibliographic records; final article full text accessed via German National Library using web tool, including DIC Methods and finite-strain formulation; official public DIC dataset landing page. Local PDF download did not succeed.
entries.relevance: Direct soft-cutting comparison combining optical deformation measurements and a model with large deformation, fracture and interface effects; public DIC data can support an external comparison.
entries.limitation: Different materials and geometry; reported friction/adhesion contributions are conditional on that model and experiment. Does not establish this project surface-address accuracy or justify fitting measured motion to FE.
entries.rights: Article CC BY 4.0. Alternate PDF is an unmodified publisher article archived by the German National Library. The approximately 1.1 GB dataset was not downloaded.

entries.title: Cutting resistance of soft materials: Effects of blade inclination and friction
entries.evidence_scope: Publisher abstract and institution bibliographic record; institutional copy explicitly closed access.
entries.relevance: Direct oblique-cutting experiments on soft elastomeric plates analyze blade inclination, insertion forces and frictional dissipation.
entries.limitation: Steady cutting force interpretation is not an estimator of original-surface point identity or initiation offset; inclination geometry must be matched before comparison.
entries.rights: Publisher subscription article; institution lists all rights reserved and closed copy. No access request or paywall bypass.

entries.title: Probing the micromechanics of a multi-contact interface at the onset of frictional sliding
entries.evidence_scope: Publisher bibliographic record and abstract; authors arXiv full preprint.
entries.relevance: DIC-based local displacement reveals coexisting stick/slip regions during incipient frictional sliding, motivating local interface motion instead of a whole-body scalar.
entries.limitation: Transparent rough PDMS/glass contact with optical access; no cutting crack and no opaque blade occlusion. Its stress inversion and friction law must not be transferred directly to this experiment.
entries.rights: Author arXiv reading copy; follow paper-specific license; distinct from final publisher version.

entries.title: Incremental calculation for large deformation measurement using reliability-guided digital image correlation
entries.evidence_scope: Publisher abstract and complete publicly hosted primary paper reviewed; especially introduction, section 2.3 reference updates and section 3 foam-compression experiment.
entries.relevance: Conditional reference updates provide a documented route around direct initial-to-current decorrelation; fewer updates limit accumulation of interpolation and incremental errors.
entries.limitation: Foam compression is not blade contact with oil and occlusion. This paper does not prove the current project dual-reference chain, recoverability, or drift-free material identity.
entries.rights: Elsevier article. Public reading link does not grant redistribution rights. No PDF is committed.
